**What I found:** Don't move `src/orders/billing.js` yet. Wait until the commit history and a complexity measurement show whether the move helps (the record calls this DEFER). The only evidence that billing changes weekly is your statement. This directory isn't a git repository, so I couldn't check whether billing edits really happen on their own, apart from the rest of orders.

**Why it matters:** The move would be cheap to undo: only `src/orders/index.js` imports billing, and there's one deployable and no stored data involved. But if billing edits usually come with `index.js` edits, a separate subsystem just splits one change across two places. If billing does change on its own, the file already keeps that churn out of orders. A move would mostly add ownership and enforceable rules, and a smaller option may give you those: make billing a nested part of orders with its own public entry point.

**Do this first:**
1. In the real repository, run `git log --since="26 weeks ago" --name-only --format=%H -- src/orders` and work out what share of the commits touching `billing.js` also touch other files under `src/orders/`. Compare it with the thresholds in `Decision policy` below.
2. Run `/alchemy C` on the two candidates to get the complexity measurement the record lists as `Not run`.
3. Re-run `/alchemy L` with both results.

**What I did not check:**
- Commit history, because this directory has no git: run step 1 in the real repository.
- The complexity measurement, because a focused L run doesn't include C: `/alchemy C`.
- Functional correctness. `placeOrder` stores a total without tax, while `reprice` adds tax. That may or may not be intended, and no tests exist yet. Check with `/code-review`, and add tests (`npm test` currently runs nothing).
